user_input: what are the 12 regional banks within the Federal Reserve System?
model_output:
The Federal Reserve System is comprised of 12 regional banks, each responsible for the operation of the Federal Reserve in their respective regions. The 12 regional banks are:
1. Federal Reserve Bank of New York (NY)
2. Federal Reserve Bank of Boston (BOS)
3. Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia (PHL)
4. Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland (CLE)
5. Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond (RIC)
6. Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta (ATL)
7. Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago (CHI)
8. Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (STL)
9. Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis (MIN)
10. Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City (KAN)
11. Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas (DAL)
12. Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco (SF)
The Federal Reserve System is the central banking system of the United States and was established in 1913. The Federal Reserve Banks are responsible for implementing the monetary policy of the Federal Reserve, supervising and regulating banks in their regions, and serving as a lender of last resort to banks in their districts.
